summary_table.content: Anorectal Canal (dorsally). • Perineal Body: Fusion site of urorectal septum with cloacal membrane; splits membrane into Urogenital & Anal membranes. • Vesical Part (Cranial): Forms Body & Apex of Urinary Bladder; continuous with allantois / urachus. • Pelvic Part (Middle): Forms lower prostatic & membranous urethra in males; entire urethra (4 cm) in females. • Phallic Part (Caudal): Forms spongy urethra (shaft) in males; vestibule of vagina in females. • Navicular Fossa: Formed by ectodermal ingrowth from the glans penis tip (canalization).

• Bladder Trigone Origin: Derived from incorporated caudal Mesoderm of mesonephric (Wolffian) ducts (later overgrown by endoderm). • Ejaculatory Ducts: Caudal ends of mesonephric ducts migrate to enter prostatic urethra at colliculus seminalis. • Prostate Gland: Endodermal outgrowths from prostatic urethra; fibromuscular stroma from splanchnic mesenchyme. • Homologues: Cowper's glands (male) = Bartholin's glands (female); Skene's glands (female) = Prostate gland (male). • Patent Urachus (Urachal Fistula): Complete failure of allantois/urachus to obliterate -> continuous urine leakage from

umbilicus from birth. • Urachal Cyst: Middle third remains patent -> painful fluid-filled midline mass between umbilicus & pubic symphysis. • Urachal Sinus: Umbilical end remains patent -> blind pouch at umbilicus prone to purulent infection. • Urachal Diverticulum: Vesical end remains patent -> blind outpouching at bladder apex. • Exstrophy of Bladder (Ectopia Vesicae): Failure of lateral body wall mesoderm migration -> anterior abdominal defect,

exposed extroverted bladder mucosa leaking urine; strongly associated with Epispadias. • Hypospadias: Failure of fusion of urethral (urogenital) folds on ventral penile shaft (1:300 males). • Posterior Urethral Valves (PUV): Thick mucosal folds in prostatic urethra; #1 cause of neonatal bladder outlet obstruction; yields 'keyhole sign' on US & oligohydramnios. • Weigert-Meyer Law: Duplex ureter upper pole moiety inserts ectopic/inferomedial with ureterocele; lower pole moiety inserts orthotopic with VUR.
